topic.name: The Shell Method: Rotation About the Y-Axis

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=5x^3+5x^2$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 5x^3+5x^2 &= 0\\[5pt] x^2(x+1) &=0 \end{align*} The solutions are $x=-1$, $x=0.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=-1$ to $x=0.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x\, f(x) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{-1}^{0} x\left( 5x^3+5x^2 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 10\pi \int_{-1}^{0} \left( x^4+x^3 \right) \textrm{d}x \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Volume of a Solid Using the Shell Method

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=16x-16x^2+4x^3$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 16x-16x^2+4x^3 &= 0 \\[5pt] 4x(x^2-4x+4) &= 0 \\[5pt] 4x(x-2)^2 &= 0 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x\, f(x) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{2} x \left( 16x-16x^2+4x^3 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{2} \left( 16x^2-16x^3+4x^4 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 8\pi \int_{0}^{2} \left( 4x^2-4x^3+x^4 \right) \textrm{d}x \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Volume of a Solid Using the Shell Method

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded between the curves $y=3-x$ and $y=x^2-6x+9.$ Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
First, let $f(x)=3-x$ and $g(x)=x^2-6x+9.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f(x) &= g(x) \\[3pt] 3-x &=x^2-6x+9 \\[3pt] x^2-5x+6 &=0 \\[3pt] \left(x - 2 \right) \left(x - 3 \right) &= 0 \end{align*}

The solutions are $x=2$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=2$ to $x=3.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=x^2-6x+9,$ and

  • leaves through the upper function $y=f(x)=3-x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x \big( \big[ {\color{brown}\text{upper}} \big] - \big[ {\color{blue}\text{lower}} \big] \big) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{2}^{3} x \left( [{\color{brown}3-x}] - [{\color{blue}x^2-6x+9}] \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \int_2^3 x(-x^2+5x-6) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \int_2^3 \left( -x^3+5x^2-6x \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \left. \left(-\dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{5x^3}{3} -3x^2\right) \right|_2^3 \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \left[ \left(- \dfrac{81}{4} +45 - 27\right) - \left(- 4 +\dfrac{40}{3}- 12\right) \right] \\[5pt] &= 2\pi\left( -\dfrac{9}{4} - \left( -\dfrac{8}{3} \right) \right)\\[5pt] &= 2\pi \cdot \dfrac{5}{12} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {5\pi}{6} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Volume of a Solid When a Region is Enclosed Between Two Curves

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded between the curves $y=2x$ and $y=5x-x^2.$ Calculate the volume $V$ of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, let $f(x)=2x$ and $g(x)=5x-x^2.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f(x) &= g(x) \\[5pt] 2x &= 5x-x^2 \\[5pt] x^2- 3x &= 0 \\[5pt] x \left(x - 3 \right) &= 0 \end{align*}

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=3.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=2x,$ and

  • leaves through the upper function $y=f(x)=5x-x^2.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x \big( \big[ {\color{brown}\text{upper}} \big] - \big[ {\color{blue}\text{lower}} \big] \big) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{3} x \left( [{\color{brown}5x-x^2}] - [{\color{blue}2x}] \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \int_0^3 x(3x-x^2) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \int_0^3 \left( 3x^2-x^3 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \left. \left(x^3 - \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right) \right|_0^3 \\[5pt] & = 2\pi \left[ \left(27- \dfrac{81}{4}\right) - 0 \right] \\[5pt] & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{27\pi}{2}} \end{align*}
